## From a Book Argument to a Reproducible Calculation

UpstreamDrift provides a possible implementation companion for studying golf mechanics and control.
A useful exercise links a specific mathematical question to a declared model, executable procedure and inspectable result.
Installing an engine or producing an animation establishes much less than validating an argument about a human swing.

This guide distinguishes three sources of information: the provider snapshot published through AffineDrift's companion catalog, each engine's own documentation, and proposed educational experiments.
The [book index](../books/index.html) links the available manuscripts and states their provisional status; the series is not simply an unpublished future plan.
Scaffolded notebook links remain distinct from executed and reviewed calculations.

## Provider Snapshot and Access

The installed companion snapshot identifies UpstreamDrift commit `27b6eeadbbd970bebb8926a3c83aeaea1f6ee4da` and manifest SHA-256 `a1c9a799ecceb4e81f28c50755fb50ad28f390ed8db335b64ecb89028f910b06`.
Its publication state is **draft** and its engine entries are scientifically **unqualified**: the catalog records installation/support categories, not numerical or biomechanical validation.
Consult the [freshness dashboard](../models/programming/freshness.html) and [engine matrix](../models/programming/engines.html) before using these facts for another revision.
The snapshot is not a claim about the latest repository state.

The repository is [D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift).
Availability depends on repository permissions; organization membership alone is not a universal access guarantee.
Public AffineDrift explanations and engine documentation can still be read independently of provider access.

| Engine | Support Category in This Snapshot | What That Entry Establishes |
|---|---|---|
| MuJoCo | Supported | Provider-listed support category |
| Drake | Extended | Provider-listed optional integration category |
| Pinocchio | Extended | Provider-listed optional integration category |
| OpenSim | Experimental | Provider-listed experimental integration category |
| MyoSuite | Experimental | Provider-listed experimental integration category |

These categories do not certify particular model assets, device backends, clinical fidelity or tested operation on every operating system.
The snapshot lists Python 3.11 and 3.12 as supported minors.
An engine's current package requirements can differ from that older provider environment; construct and record a compatible environment rather than mixing versions implicitly.

## What the Engines Contribute

### MuJoCo: Forward Simulation and Contact

MuJoCo supplies rigid-body simulation with model-dependent joints, actuators and contact.
The ordinary `mujoco.mj_step` interface should not be described as automatically running GPU-accelerated dynamics.
[MuJoCo's MJX documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/mjx.html) describes separate accelerator implementations and their feature and performance differences.
A calculation must identify which backend actually executed, along with its precision, timestep, solver settings and model.

Zeroing actuator commands does not automatically produce a gravity-only system.
Damping, elastic forces, contact, actuator state and external forces may remain.
For a passive-swing exercise, specify exactly which terms and boundary conditions are retained.
Do not infer a shoulder angle from `qpos[0]` without checking the model's joint ordering and configuration representation.

### Drake: Modeling, Optimization and Controller Design

Drake offers multibody modeling and numerical optimization facilities, including trajectory-optimization tools.
A successfully solved direct-collocation problem does not itself prove continuous-time constraint satisfaction, global optimality or robust stabilization.
Check defects, constraint residuals, mesh sensitivity and an independent rollout; controller validation adds another task.
A formal certificate requires its own assumptions and verification procedure.

Use the current [installation matrix](https://drake.mit.edu/installation.html) and [parser API](https://drake.mit.edu/pydrake/pydrake.multibody.parsing.html) for the selected release.
Current parser documentation uses `AddModels`; choose the signature documented for the installed version.
DDP and iLQR are algorithm families, not a capability guaranteed by listing Drake as an engine.
Name and verify the actual implementation used in an exercise.

### Pinocchio: Kinematics and Recursive Dynamics

Pinocchio provides rigid-body kinematics, Jacobians, inverse dynamics and articulated-body forward dynamics.
Linear-time recursion applies to specified tree algorithms with bounded joint dimension; it is not a universal complexity claim for every query, dense matrix output or constrained solve.
The [project's installation instructions](https://github.com/stack-of-tasks/pinocchio) distinguish the pip distribution **`pin`** from the Python import **`pinocchio`** and the conda package **`pinocchio`**.

For supported environments, the project documents:

```bash
python -m pip install pin
# Alternative package manager:
conda install pinocchio -c conda-forge
```

Choose one installation route and follow its current platform guidance.
These commands identify the package; they are not a pinned provider environment or a record of installation tests performed for this article.

When adapting a model example, use a valid configuration on its manifold, check that the requested frame exists, and state the Jacobian's point and reference frame.
An all-zero coordinate array can be invalid for quaternion joints.
Configuration storage size `nq` can differ from tangent-velocity size `nv`; the [dimensionality article](degrees-of-freedom-and-dimensionality.html) explains why storage count and physical dimension differ.
A six-row spatial Jacobian combines angular and linear quantities: a norm or singular-value comparison needs an explicit scaling convention.

### OpenSim and MyoSuite: Muscle Models and Learning Tasks

[OpenSim](https://opensim.stanford.edu/) supports musculoskeletal modeling and analysis.
Muscle force depends on the chosen constitutive model, geometry, activation, length, velocity and tendon state.
Inverse dynamics supplies net generalized loads under model and data assumptions; it does not uniquely identify individual muscle forces.

[MyoSuite's tutorials](https://myosuite.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials.html) provide muscle-driven environments and examples using its Gym interface.
Use an environment ID documented for the installed release and inspect that release's reset and step signatures.
Resolve each model through its provider catalog rather than inventing a golf asset path or environment ID.
Muscle actuator counts must not be called joint degrees of freedom, and a library's reaching or hand task does not establish a validated golf environment.
A trained reinforcement-learning policy reflects its task, observation model, reward, training distribution and simulator; biological plausibility needs additional evidence.

## Start With a Governed Workflow

At the pinned provider revision, the catalog lists `installation-verification` as an available workflow with this entry point:

```bash
# Run inside the provider checkout at the declared snapshot revision.
python -m scripts.companion_workflows execute --workflow-id installation-verification
```

The workflow's declared prerequisites include Python 3.11 or 3.12 and that exact checkout.
Its scope is the Python floor and provider-authority imports; optional GUI and engine extras are outside it.
An exit code of zero therefore does not mean all engines or models were installed or scientifically validated.
This review checks the published command contract, not a fresh execution of the provider workflow.

The same snapshot lists reference double-pendulum simulation and analysis, simulation plotting/reporting and a zero-torque counterfactual workflow.
Use the [programming companion](../models/programming/index.html) to inspect prerequisites, model identifiers, expected artifacts and limitations for the selected workflow.
An available catalog entry is not proof that a particular machine has run it successfully.
Do not substitute guessed file paths or an undocumented Python module for the published contract.

For each exercise, retain the provider and model revision, dependency versions, parameter units, coordinates, initial conditions, controls, contact assumptions, solver settings and output hashes.
Record failures as failures.
Compare against an analytical identity or a separate numerical formulation where possible, then vary timestep, tolerances and relevant parameters.
This connects implementation evidence to a bounded statement about the modeled motion.

## Learning Sequence and Book Connections

| Reading | Educational Question | Evidence to Produce |
|---|---|---|
| Volume 0, Chapters 2–4 | What are the state, configuration and rotation conventions? | A declared coordinate map, valid rotations and consistent velocity dimensions |
| Volume 0, Chapters 7 and 10 | How does recursive dynamics compute the same acceleration? | Matched-model ABA versus a separate equations-of-motion calculation; a declared timing protocol |
| Volume I, Chapters 2 and 4 | How do perturbations evolve near a trajectory? | Variational predictions compared with finite perturbations over a specified horizon |
| Volume I, Chapters 7–8 | What changes under a specified control intervention? | A declared intervention, matching initial conditions and model-conditioned output differences |
| Volume II, Chapters 4–6 | Is the problem orbital stabilization or finite-time trajectory design? | A valid periodic orbit and return map, or a finite-horizon optimization and verified rollout |
| Volume III | Which biological parameters can observations identify? | Sensitivity and uncertainty analysis under a stated muscle/contact model |
| Volume IV | What distinguishes competing coordination hypotheses? | Explicit alternative controllers and independent tests; reconstruction accuracy alone is insufficient |
| Volume V | How is a model study made repeatable? | Revision-bound inputs, procedures, artifacts and acceptance limits |

These are proposed exercises, not a promise that every chapter already has a runnable companion implementation.
The sequence starts with coordinate and numerical checks because more elaborate inference depends on them.
A model can animate smoothly while using the wrong sign, reference point or actuator interpretation.

## Three Interpretation Checks

### Drift-Control Ratio

For a chosen control-affine model and a positive-definite metric $M$, one possible instantaneous convention is

$$\rho(x,u)=\frac{\|f(x)\|_M}{\|G(x)u\|_M}.$$

The norm is $\|z\|_M=\sqrt{z^T Mz}$ for state-derivative vectors expressed in the chosen coordinates.

This requires a nonzero denominator; report zero-control cases explicitly rather than hiding them in an arbitrary offset.
If both contributions vanish, the ratio is indeterminate.
Declare state scaling, metric, input baseline and which part of the state derivative is being compared.
A ratio of acceleration contributions is a different definition from a ratio of full state derivatives.
For nonlinear muscle activation dynamics, first establish whether the selected inputs produce a control-affine model at all.

A large ratio is not an energy fraction or proof that control is unimportant.
A small control contribution can be decisive for trajectory direction or terminal accuracy.
This guide establishes no measured expert-swing threshold for $\rho$.

### Perturbation Decay and Contraction

Fitting decay to a finite collection of simulated trajectory separations is a diagnostic on those samples.
A contraction certificate requires a metric inequality over a declared domain, including state dependence and invariance conditions.
Even a constant stable linear system can grow transiently in Euclidean distance.
For example,

$$A=\begin{bmatrix}-1&10\\0&-1\end{bmatrix}$$

has eigenvalues $-1$, while $(A+A^T)/2$ has a positive eigenvalue $4$.
Thus an LQR closed-loop pole location is not generally a Euclidean contraction rate.
The chosen metric, nonlinear operating region and perturbation norm must be specified before comparing theoretical and simulated rates.

### Floquet Analysis and Impact Events

Floquet analysis requires a periodic reference with the corresponding variational dynamics.
For an autonomous periodic orbit, distinguish the neutral phase multiplier from transverse stability.
Hybrid periodic motion also requires the event/reset sensitivity in the return-map derivative.
A finite downswing followed by ball impact does not automatically supply a periodic orbit; finite-horizon sensitivities or terminal-error propagation are usually the first questions to formulate.
These distinctions follow the [orbital-stability treatment](https://underactuated.csail.mit.edu/limit_cycles.html) and the [transverse-contraction literature](https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.4433), not the name of a simulation engine.

The educational payoff is a traceable chain: a mathematical statement determines what should be computed, the model determines what that computation means, and validation determines how far its conclusion can travel.
Moving from a successful calculation to an explanation of a golfer requires evidence beyond the calculation itself.
